title: Northstar capacity cadence ops sketch - weekly
content:
Context: quick working notes from this week's capacity cadence (Northstar ops + regional leads). Intention is to capture the anomalies, experiment outcomes, proposed playbook edits, and a prioritized TODO list. Treat as informal — lots of open questions.

Attendees: Aisha K (notes), Diego R, Mei C, Owen P, Samira E, Priya (SRE), Luca (serving-runtime).

1) What we observed this week
- Global GPU pool utilization (weighted by capacity): 68% avg (7d window). Trend: +6% week-over-week.
- Spike event (2026-03-26 14:00 UTC): us-west-2 p95 latency jumped to 1.9s for generation route. Root cause: short-lived surge from a marketing demo + 3 long-running embeddings batches that bypassed burst guard.
- Preemptible churn: 12 preemptions in ap-southeast-1 over 48h (higher than baseline 3/day). Likely due to cloud provider maintenance window. Impact: 4 customers saw failed requests with no graceful fallback.
- Backfill experiment A/B summary (see linked PR):
  - A (current heuristic): backfill allowed when queue < 200ms and node idle > 8s. Result: higher utilization but occasional tail latency regressions during mixed small/long inference workloads.
  - B (randomized-stagger backfill): inserts jitter and enforces a soft cap per-node of 3 concurrent backfills. Result: p99 latency improved by ~18% in us-west, but mean utilization dropped ~4%.
  - Team takeaway: B reduces customer-facing tails but costs a bit more. Need ROI calc (cost vs SLA improvements).

2) Regional notes and proposals
- us-west-2: short-term config: enable backfill-B for 6am-6pm PST experiment window for next two business days. Measure p95/p99 and failed requests.
- eu-central-1: steady; consider moving one burst pool from east to eu to reduce cross-region routing. Action: Diego to propose migration window (ETA 2026-04-02).
- ap-southeast-1: investigate preemption mitigation. Proposal: raise minimum reserved non-preemptible nodes to 6 during vendor-maintenance windows (weekends). Action: Mei to confirm cost delta and vendor maintenance schedule.

3) Priming and warm-pool experiment notes
- Small warm-pool priming (keep 1 hot replica per 4 nodes for high-traffic models) reduced cold-start latency by ~220ms on average for the tested model set. But warm-pool increases baseline cost by ~1.6%.
- Question: do we keep warm-pool for top-10 models only, or expand based on usage heatmap? Suggestion: run tiered priming for 2 weeks: top-10 full warm, next-20 soft-warm (KV cache only). Owen volunteered to sketch policy rules.

4) Playbook edits (quick draft items)
- Add 'marketing-demo' tag that triggers temporary stricter burst-guard for a customer-defined demo window. Rationale: last spike came from an internal demo that bypassed normal throttles.
- Add explicit preemption response routine: if preemptions > 5 in 1h in a region, automatically shift 10% of new CIDR allocations to dedicated (non-preemptible) pool until 6h after last preemption. (SRE to sign off).
- Backfill policy: prefer randomized-stagger B for production-critical routes; allow A for experimental routes where throughput trumps tail latency.

5) Action items and owners
- Diego R: schedule east->eu burst pool handoff proposal (due 2026-04-02).
- Mei C: vendor maintenance calendar + preemptible mitigation cost estimate (due 2026-03-31).
- Owen P: draft tiered priming policy and config knobs for console toggles (due 2026-04-06).
- Samira E: update incident runbook with preemption detection and auto-shift steps (draft by 2026-03-30).
- Aisha K: run quick ROI calc for backfill-B vs. SLA lift (deliverable: short note + numbers by 2026-03-31).

6) Open questions / discussion backlog (notes-to-self)
- How do we quantify user experience lift vs extra cost of warm-pools? Need to instrument a UX proxy (delta in p50/p95 perceived by end app).
- Is randomized backfill+B stable under mixed long-running and short-running model mixes? We need more cross-region runs and to include embeddings-heavy workloads.
- What is the right default for demo tagging? Should product own the tag or infra expose simple API to opt-in?

7) Quick logs / snippets from the incident (for post-mortem)
- 2026-03-26 13:57 UTC: alert threshold crossed: generation p95 > 1.2s (auto escalated).
- 2026-03-26 14:04 UTC: routing fallback engaged to model-small (compatible variant) for 2% of requests. No major customer impact but visible degradation for demo user.
- 2026-03-26 14:27 UTC: manual throttle applied to demo CID. Root cause traced to a mis-configured demo token that bypassed quota checks.

8) Notes for next week's cadence
- Run 48h randomized-backfill B in us-west only (A/B telemetry ready).
- Prepare short briefing for product about demo-token policy and proposed opt-in model.
- Start collecting a 14-day heatmap for warm-pool candidates.

Misc quick scribbles
- Consider adding a "demo sandbox" feature that isolates marketing demos from production routing entirely (low friction, short lived).
- Meeting habit: next cadence, bring one customer-success rep to hear the demo impact directly.

End of sketch.

-- Aisha
